label: pjm 32 refconvex
definition: (PROBE - structural diagnostic, NOT a keeper). pjm_28 keeper config but the interchange seam is served by the forecast-grade REFERENCE-PRICE interface (replaces the fitted, per-year EXPORT_TRANCHES with each neighbor priced (HenryHub+basis) x marginal_HR x (load/mean)^exp) PLUS neighbor price-vs-load CONVEXITY load_shape_exponent=1.63 - self-derived from NYISO's own realized RT LMP (log-LMP on log-load, R2 0.36, stable 1.64/1.63 by year), adopted for MISO/Carolinas as the organized-thermal-neighbor value (cross-validated NEISO 2.04 / ERCOT-net 1.47) pending their own-LMP fetch. Nothing tuned to PJM's net-MWh (claude.md #11). RESULT: the seam LIFTS energy LMP toward actual every year - 2023 -1.1%->+4.0% (29.57 vs 28.44), 2024 -7.7%->-4.1% (28.32 vs 29.53), 2025 -16.8%->-10.5% (38.40 vs 42.89) - confirming the missing summer-afternoon $75-200 regime was peak-coincident export tightening. BUT the convexity self-limits the over-export only partway (pjm_31 +78 -> +62 TWh in 2023): net export flips from pjm_28's UNDER (-46/-24/-46%) to OVER (+56/+34/+112%, actual 40.0/32.7/18.0), and the excess export over-generates fossil (gas 2024 +6.9% / 2025 +7.0% FAIL; coal-tot 2023 +9.4% / 2025 +9.5% FAIL; 7 in-tol fails vs pjm_28's 0). 2025 is worst (+112%): the single 2023-24 neighbor HR anchors miss 2025's collapsed PJM-neighbor spread. NEXT LEVER (data-driven, no fit): (1) fetch MISO Indiana-Hub + Duke LMP -> derive each dominant seam's OWN convexity (likely steeper than NYISO's 1.63, self-limiting more); (2) year-grounded neighbor HR anchor from each neighbor's own per-year realized-LMP/gas ratio to compress the 2025 spread. pjm_28 stays the keeper until the over-export is bounded by these.
